Extract transit network in sf format

Source: R/network_tools.R
transit_network_to_sf.Rd

The public transport network in sf format: the stops of the 'GTFS' feeds, and the line of every trip pattern of each route.

Usage

transit_network_to_sf(network)

Arguments

network

A network built with build_network().

Value

A list with two sf data frames in WGS 84: stops (POINT), with columns stop_index, stop_id (prefixed by the feed id), stop_name, linked_to_street and geometry, and routes (LINESTRING), with columns agency_id, agency_name, route_id, long_name, short_name, mode and geometry. There is one route row per trip pattern (the trips of a route with the same stops), so the same route can appear more than once; its line is the GTFS shape of the first trip of the pattern or, without one, the positions of its stops. A stop not linked to the street network (outside the area of the .pbf, for instance) has an empty geometry (POINT EMPTY), and a pattern with no line is left out. Positions of stops are those of their vertices in the street network (the coordinates rounded down to 1e-7 degrees). Package 'sf' is needed. With options(peabiru.output = "data.table"), routes is an sf data.table and stops a plain sf data frame (see peabiru-package).

See also

Other network functions: build_network(), check_transit_availability(), find_snap(), get_gtfs_errors(), street_network_bbox(), street_network_to_sf()

Examples

data_path <- system.file("extdata/spo", package = "peabiru")
network <- build_network(data_path, n_threads = 2)
transit_net <- transit_network_to_sf(network)
head(transit_net$stops)
